applicability_conditions: The test medium is aqueous and contains available iron(III).
The phenolic hydroxy group is structurally accessible.
The observed colour is distinct from the iron(III) reagent blank.
rule.claim: In aqueous media where iron(III) remains available for coordination, an accessible phenolic hydroxy group can form a visibly colored iron(III)-phenol or iron(III)-phenolate complex.
exclusions: This forward rule is not an unconditional colour-implies-phenol inverse.
A negative result does not exclude every phenol.
Precipitation, incompatible pH, or competing strong ligands are outside scope.
The rule does not identify a particular molecule.

source.locator: Nature 165 (1950) 1012, complete one-page letter; absorption and titration study of freshly prepared aqueous ferric chloride-phenol coloured complexes.

applicability_conditions: One exact input-source locator binds every one of these cues to the same unknown compound D and metal Q: anhydrous C reacts with excess NaF to yield D, D contains displayed mass fractions of 32.85% sodium and 12.85% Q, and D is used in industrial production of Q.

Before nomination, a source-first staged-species audit enumerates every allowed solid input and output, volatile or other byproduct, and external input, and binds every admitted element to the problem source or a separately sealed authority; anonymous material streams and mere failure to mention another constituent are insufficient.

That audit affirmatively closes D as one anhydrous, neutral, stoichiometric phase with complete element domain exactly Na, Q, and F; closes anhydrous C as one Q/F phase; and establishes NaF as the only external sodium-bearing input to the directed C-to-D stage.

The cited EPA process statement is used only to nominate the exact candidate pair aluminum and stoichiometric cryolite Na3AlF6 within that closed domain; it is not treated as an exhaustive inventory of every substance used by industry.

Using controller-pinned atomic weights and their uncertainties, the audit checks the candidate's complete unrounded molar mass, sodium fraction, Q fraction, fluorine remainder, charge balance, and primitive integer stoichiometry against both source-displayed two-decimal mass intervals without candidate-shaped tolerances or staged rounding.

The identities and formulas of C and its hydrate are not imported from the EPA source: after the D candidate is retained, a separate source-led atom and charge ledger must balance the directed anhydrous-C plus NaF stage, and a finite positive-integer hydrate audit must uniquely satisfy the displayed water-mass interval.

Every candidate admitted by the declared finite domain is subjected to the same complete audits; if another candidate passes, or a coefficient, oxidation-state, element, phase, or hydrate bound is solver-created rather than source-bound, the result remains underdetermined.

The current bridge obligation records the exact problem locators, complete staged-species domain, candidate inventory, pinned-constant receipts, raw interval calculations, balanced reaction ledger, and every exclusion so that no applicability condition depends on an open-world absence assumption.
rule.claim: Within an explicitly closed, source-bounded domain satisfying every listed condition, the source-stated conjunction that a sodium-metal-fluoride compound is used in industrial production of the same metal may use the cited EPA fact only to nominate the candidate pair aluminum and stoichiometric cryolite Na3AlF6 for a bounded filter. That candidate may be retained only when the independent complete composition, charge, primitive-stoichiometry, reaction-ledger, and displayed-mass-interval audit passes uniquely.
exclusions: This policy is not the universal inverse used-in-production-of-Q implies cryolite or aluminum.
The EPA source does not identify an open-world unknown, construct or close the problem's candidate domain, or prove that cryolite is the only material used in aluminum production.
Cryolite is the electrolyte and solvent in the cited primary-aluminum process; the rule does not make it the aluminum-bearing feedstock, the sole bath component, or a reagent that must be consumed.

Actual baths containing aluminum fluoride, calcium fluoride, lithium salts, dissolved alumina, excess components, mixtures, dopants, substituted phases, or nonstoichiometric cryolite do not establish that an unknown compound is pure Na3AlF6.

The source establishes neither the identity or formula of C, the hydrate number, reaction completeness, a sole-product claim, phase purity, element closure, oxidation state, nor any unprinted protocol detail.
Mass agreement alone cannot select a candidate, supply a missing constituent, impose an arbitrary coefficient bound, or exclude an unenumerated alternative.

The policy does not apply to secondary-aluminum processing, aluminum-chloride electrolysis, production of another metal, or a use clue that is absent, ambiguous, or bound to a different compound or metal.
Any missing staged-species record, any unclassified material stream, any incompatible source cue, or any second passing candidate makes the policy inapplicable and the target must fail closed.

source.locator: U.S. EPA AP-42, Fifth Edition, Volume I, Section 12.1.2.2, printed pages 12.1-1 to 12.1-2: the Hall-Heroult process produces aluminum metal, and molten cryolite (Na3AlF6) functions as the electrolyte and solvent for alumina.

applicability_conditions: An independently source-bound exact-carbon-count derivation, using no iron(III)-response premise, establishes a finite and explicitly closed candidate domain.
The problem authors explicitly label a positive aqueous iron(III) colour response as characteristic; the exact positive-response text and test-condition locator are recorded.

Every candidate's complete source-bound structure is audited for an accessible phenolic hydroxy group, and each structural-feature assignment is traceable to problem text or separately sealed evidence.

For a candidate without an accessible phenolic hydroxy group, every functionality relevant to the response is source-bound and lies within this fixed non-phenolic whitelist: unactivated aliphatic alcohol, saturated ether, hydrocarbon, or simple non-chelating monoketone.

The source-bound candidate audit establishes that no candidate contains a beta-dicarbonyl or enol, hydroxamate, catecholate-like group, other explicitly iron-binding ligand, or unclassified functionality relevant to the response.

The test-condition audit checks the explicit aqueous iron(III) cue and that the problem source does not explicitly state an incompatible pH, strong ligand, precipitation branch, alternative reagent, or nonselective branch; it does not require or infer unstated test details.

The current bridge obligation records the closed domain, independent exact-carbon derivation, characteristic positive cue, every candidate structure and whitelist classification, and the test-condition audit so each condition can be checked without a solver-created category or open-world absence assumption.
rule.claim: Within an independently exact-carbon-derived finite closed candidate domain satisfying every listed condition, a positive aqueous iron(III) colour response that the problem authors explicitly label as characteristic may be used only as a bounded filter between candidates with a source-audited accessible phenolic hydroxy group and candidates whose response-relevant functionality lies entirely within the fixed non-phenolic whitelist.
exclusions: This policy is not a universal colour-implies-phenol chemical law.
It does not identify an open-world unknown, construct the candidate set, infer the carbon count, or establish that the domain is closed.

It does not authorize inference when the characteristic label is solver-supplied, the response is negative or ambiguous, the medium is not source-bound as aqueous, or any required source-stated cue or required audit is missing.
Any beta-dicarbonyl or enol, hydroxamate, catecholate-like group, other explicitly iron-binding ligand, or unclassified response-relevant functionality makes this policy inapplicable.
The fixed whitelist cannot be expanded by a candidate, solver, or Reviewer, and classification by mere failure to find an interferent is insufficient.
It does not infer unstated pH, ligand concentration, solubility, selectivity, reagent identity, or other experimental detail.
It does not use a negative test to exclude every phenol.
The cited study reports selectivity only for its tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol; it does not itself establish this policy for arbitrary candidate domains.
The cue alone does not identify a particular molecule or authorize any conclusion outside the audited finite domain.

source.locator: Journal of the Japan Society of Colour Material 35(2) (1962) 59-61; page 59 abstract and page 61 discussion and conclusion, limited to the tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol.

applicability_conditions: One exact input-source locator binds all of these cues to the same observation: thermogravimetric analysis, an unambiguous stated atmosphere, a later mass-loss event, wording that names the ensuing mass as final, a named single compound assigned to that mass, and a statement that its mass remains constant at higher temperatures.

The conjunctive named-final cue is accepted only as a bounded terminal-product stipulation under explicit closed contest semantics; a plateau, stable mass, or high-temperature constancy without every cue in the preceding condition is insufficient.

The current source bundle either contains a controller-authenticated fallback for each prior-part conclusion or the redraft transparently rederives the starting material's metal identity and charge, the organic anion's identity and charge, and the stoichiometric salt core from bound prior-part sources; this policy identifies none of them, and a prior-part question or label, material name, or occurrence alone establishes none of them.

Every earlier mass-loss stage is represented in a source-led mass ledger. If an earlier stage is used to identify a volatile component or unchanged intermediate, that identity and completeness are established independently; the conjunctive named-final cue supplies neither.

The pinned Treccani source is used only as qualitative corroboration that a source-led starting candidate within its exact material scope can leave the residue class described there; it is not used as a thermogravimetric record or as a quantitative conversion premise.

A finite closed candidate audit enumerates every primitive neutral integer terminal-residue formula compatible with the independently established element and oxidation-state domain, then checks atom, charge, and every measured-mass interval using pinned constants and source uncertainties.

Every possible counterion, dopant, container, reagent, and alternative atmosphere contribution is affirmatively excluded by source-bounded evidence or an explicit closed-domain stipulation; mere failure to mention one is insufficient.
rule.claim: Within an explicitly closed source-bounded domain satisfying every listed condition, the source's conjunctive named-final cue may be used only to retain a primitive neutral terminal-residue formula candidate that passes the complete atom, charge, and measured-mass interval audit.
exclusions: This policy is not a paper or universal empirical calcination law and does not identify an open-world residue.
A bare stable plateau, an ambiguous or unstated atmosphere, a mass not expressly called final, or a residue not expressly named as a single compound cannot activate the policy.
An activation receipt proves catalog integrity and redraft availability only; it does not prove that any named-final cue or other applicability condition is present.
The named-final cue does not establish the identity or completeness of any earlier dehydration, decomposition, oxidation, or volatilization step.
The Treccani observation does not establish thermogravimetric conditions, complete conversion, quantitative recovery, or a temperature-time program.
It does not authorize any specific temperature, duration, yield, purity, phase, or polymorph.
It does not authorize selection from mass agreement alone or supply missing constituents, oxidation states, candidate closure, uncertainty bounds, or exclusions.

source.locator: Piazza, Mellite, Enciclopedia Italiana (1934), sentence reporting that mellite burns in a blowpipe test and leaves an infusible alumina residue. Normalized Italian sentence SHA-256: 5b58d1ef840834a81224de8487fde93c4f09ef2ed4643f70f0e530cdc76357a5.

applicability_conditions: An exact input-source locator binds one explicit directed reaction statement in which a source-named reactant, source-named reagent, and source-named product role occur in the same clause; the direction is source-stated rather than solver-supplied.
The source omits one or more protocol details, and every omitted detail is recorded as unknown rather than inferred.
The identities of the reactant and reagent and the role of the product are each independently established from source-bounded evidence; this policy identifies none of them.
Every independent source constraint on the product, including composition and symmetry when supplied, is represented before candidate filtering.
A finite, explicitly closed candidate set is derived without this policy and completely audited against the directed statement and every independent source constraint.
Any empirical transformation rule used alongside this policy independently satisfies its own exact substrate, reagent, and protocol applicability conditions.
rule.claim: Within an explicitly closed source-bounded candidate set satisfying every listed condition, an explicit directed statement that a named reactant reacts with a named reagent to give a named product role may be used only as a non-exclusive positive constraint for retaining compatible candidates when protocol details are omitted.
exclusions: This policy does not infer heating, temperature, time, pressure, solvent, atmosphere, catalyst, concentration, workup, or apparatus from a missing protocol.
It does not establish yield, conversion extent, completeness, purity, isolation, mass balance, or sole or principal product status.
A literature transformation with extra conditions may not supply an omitted source condition or be treated as applicable merely because its substrate and reagent resemble the source clause.
The policy neither identifies any reactant, reagent, or product nor selects a candidate from composition, symmetry, or mass agreement alone.
It does not authorize a reverse implication, an open-world classification, a thermal-decomposition inference, or a terminal-residue inference.
The IUPAC source establishes only directional reactant-to-product semantics for a chemical reaction equation; it does not establish this bounded contest policy or any omitted protocol detail.

source.locator: IUPAC Green Book, 3rd ed., 2nd printing (2008), section 2.12.1, printed p. 68, Equations for chemical reactions: the reactant and product sides are connected by an arrow whose rightward form denotes the net forward reaction. The source does not supply omitted experimental conditions.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is exactly hexamethylbenzene.
The oxidant is potassium permanganate.
The reported cold-condition transformation is the claimed scope.
rule.claim: Under the reported cold potassium-permanganate conditions, hexamethylbenzene can be oxidized to mellitic acid.
exclusions: The record does not establish an acidic medium.
It does not generalize to arbitrary alkylbenzenes.
It does not claim a unique product, rate, or yield outside the reported protocol.

source.locator: Bulletin de la Société minéralogique de France 4 (1881) 26-28, page 26 opening paragraph.

applicability_conditions: The phase has been independently established as crystalline mellite.
The material is treated as an ideal stoichiometric phase.
rule.claim: The ideal crystalline mineral mellite has composition Al2[C6(COO)6]·16H2O, equivalently [Al(H2O)6]2·C12O12·4H2O.
exclusions: Occurrence in a coal or lignite deposit alone does not identify a sample.
Impure or nonstoichiometric material is outside scope.
This rule does not determine a thermal-decomposition residue.

source.locator: Acta Crystallographica B29 (1973) 26-31, page 26 abstract and reported single-crystal composition.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is mellitic acid.
The dehydrating reagent and heating protocol are the reported benzoyl-chloride procedure.
rule.claim: In the reported six-hour heating protocol with a large excess of benzoyl chloride, mellitic acid undergoes complete dehydration to C12O9; warm-water hydration by three water equivalents regenerates the acid.
exclusions: This record does not authorize substitution of phosphorus pentoxide.
It does not generalize to arbitrary polycarboxylic acids or dehydrating reagents.

source.locator: Berichte der deutschen chemischen Gesellschaft 46 (1913) 813-815; page 814 preparation and page 815 hydration and analysis.

applicability_conditions: The substrate is exactly mellitic acid.
The reagent is exactly phosphorus pentoxide and the mixture is heated.
The product reference is limited to the mellitic trianhydride identified by the immediately preceding discussion in the cited paper.
The claim is existential and partial: the paper's 'some' product formation is the maximum admitted extent.
rule.claim: When mellitic acid is heated with phosphorus pentoxide under the reported conditions, some mellitic trianhydride (C12O9) forms.
exclusions: The record does not establish complete or quantitative dehydration, conversion, yield, or mass balance.
It does not establish that C12O9 is the sole or principal product, or that pure trianhydride can be isolated by this procedure.
It does not generalize to another substrate, dehydrating reagent, or unreported protocol.
It is not a thermal-decomposition rule and does not identify any open-air thermogravimetric residue.
